title: prompt-collection
description: Prompts collected from X for context-aware suggestions.

prompts.title: Browser testing across widths, touch, and slow networks
prompts.use_when: A web interface needs verification across screen sizes, touch input, and slow connections.
prompts.prompt: Test this in the browser at different widths, with touch emulation, and on a throttled 3G connection. Fix anything that looks broken or feels off. Save a before and after screenshot for every fix and send me a summary afterwards.

prompts.title: End-to-end proof
prompts.use_when: A completed feature needs end-to-end evidence that it works.
prompts.prompt: test this e2e & give me irrefutable proof it works

prompts.title: Single source of truth audit
prompts.use_when: The same fact or configuration may be maintained in multiple places.
prompts.prompt: single source of truth audit

prompts.title: Full project audit
prompts.use_when: A project needs a broad review of correctness, consistency, and unnecessary work.
prompts.prompt: Read this entire project and find everything that's broken, inconsistent, inefficient, or no longer needed. Fix what you're sure about and list the rest for me to review.

prompts.title: Delete, simplify, optimize, automate
prompts.use_when: Complexity or weak assumptions make a codebase harder to maintain.
prompts.prompt:
I want you to audit our codebase, is anything here unnecessary, overly complicated in our current setup, or based on weak assumptions? Challenge them.

- What can be deleted entirely?
- What can be simplified now that unnecessary pieces are gone?

Then make the changes. Prefer deleting over simplifying, simplifying over optimizing, and optimizing over automating.

This product is being used by thousands of customers, do not cut any corners.

prompts.title: Find implicit state machines
prompts.use_when: An app has behavior that depends on changing state and events.
prompts.prompt: find all of the implicit state machines in my app

prompts.title: Make useful state machines explicit
prompts.use_when: Implicit state transitions may benefit from explicit modeling; the prompt references lavish-axi.
prompts.prompt: audit and find implicit state machines in this <codebase/directory/module> that would drive concrete improvements if made explicit. explain before/after of each one and discuss with me in lavish-axi. fewer words, big visuals

prompts.title: Recover the minimal semantic model
prompts.use_when: Async behavior, duplicated state, or refactors need semantic analysis.
prompts.prompt:
Recover my program's minimal semantic model.

1. State: every value that changes what the user sees
2. Transitions: what commutes, what's idempotent, what's order-dependent
3. Dependencies: what must be true before each effect fires

Then find:
→ nondeterminism in awaits, retries and event order
→ invariants enforced by hope
→ one fact stored in two places, drifting
→ work that never reaches the screen

Last, split my refactors into "provably equivalent" and "trust me". For each "trust me", give the smallest input that breaks it.

prompts.title: Document state machines and fix reachable bugs
prompts.use_when: Reachable invalid states need evidence, documentation, and regression-tested fixes.
prompts.prompt: Find the app’s explicit and implicit state machines and document their states, invariants, and transition tables in one file. Identify invalid states or transitions the code can actually reach, with evidence, including through retries and concurrency. Prioritize confirmed bugs by impact, group related fixes into issues, then fix them with regression tests and keep the document updated.

prompts.title: Simplicity across UX, DX, and AX
prompts.use_when: An interface or implementation feels cluttered or unnecessarily complex.
prompts.prompt: I want this to be as perfect as Linear's website or Apple Notes: simple purpose, simple architecture, simple design, simple implementation. Cut taglines, helper text and secondary labels. If a screen needs them to make sense, fix the layout. Every decision should elevate the user experience (UX), developer experience (DX) and agent experience (AX) at once, without breaking anything.

prompts.title: Select only the database fields you need
prompts.use_when: Database queries fetch whole rows while using only a few fields.
prompts.prompt: find every place we load a whole row from the database just to read a couple of fields. instead, select only what we need

prompts.title: Remove unnecessary URL parsing
prompts.use_when: Repeated or redundant URL parsing may add unnecessary work.
prompts.prompt: remove all unnecessary `new URL()` parsing

prompts.title: Compute regexes at module level
prompts.use_when: Regexes are repeatedly constructed in functions or loops.
prompts.prompt: compute all regexes at the module level instead of inside functions and loops

prompts.title: Promote hot JSONB keys to columns
prompts.use_when: A hot path repeatedly reads a single key from a large JSONB value.
prompts.prompt: find hot-path reads of a single key from a large jsonb column and promote that key to a real column

prompts.title: Remove unnecessary sequential async calls
prompts.use_when: Independent async operations appear to run sequentially on hot paths.
prompts.prompt: do a deep scan of all hot paths and fix any unnecessary sequential async function calls

prompts.title: Security audit, remediation, and dashboard
prompts.use_when: A project needs a security audit and evidence of remediation; the prompt references an external Cloudflare skill.
prompts.prompt:
Install Cloudflare’s security-audit skill globally and invoke its full audit workflow on this project.

github.com/cloudflare/sec — https://t.co/PoZZnDNiPy

Please implement this skill for my project repos or globally in my projects.

Independently verify findings, implement targeted fixes for confirmed vulnerabilities, and run relevant tests. Preserve unrelated changes.

Build an interactive security dashboard covering frontend, APIs, authentication, databases, infrastructure and dependencies. Show:
- Findings by severity and affected stack layer.
- Open, fixed and verified remediation status.
- Security posture before and after fixes.
- Source evidence, code changes and test results.
- Audit coverage, unverified areas and remaining priorities.

Base posture assessments on evidence and clearly label coverage gaps.

prompts.title: Remove unused macOS software and permissions
prompts.use_when: The user explicitly wants to review and remove unused macOS software and permissions.
prompts.prompt: remove all the apps, tcc/permission grants, login items, daemons, kexts, browser exts, homebrew packages, etc., that I don't need and use.

prompts.title: Read-only codebase simplification audit (summary)
prompts.use_when: You want evidence-backed simplification recommendations before authorizing code changes.
prompts.prompt:
Review the repository without changing it. Map its subsystems and boundaries, then examine each for worthwhile improvements to data structures, state representation, algorithms, control flow, and ownership. Use bounded, independent reviews where available. Keep a shared coverage record, including explicit decisions that no change is warranted.

Limit each subsystem to two strong recommendations, supported by file references, proposed changes, scope, risks, validation needs, and confidence. Independently check findings, remove duplicates and weak abstractions, and review coverage before ranking recommendations by impact and dependencies. Do not implement changes or run tests during the audit.

This is an editorial summary. Read the linked gist for the complete workflow.

prompts.title: Product experience coverage audit (summary)
prompts.use_when: You need a product-wide UX review with an actionable handoff for product, design, and engineering.
prompts.prompt:
Assess the current product without modifying its repository. Establish its users, goals, and constraints from workspace evidence. Track coverage of screens, states, and complete journeys, combining code inspection with safe runtime observation. Focus on desktop and tablet, including keyboard, touch, accessibility, and recovery behavior; phone optimization is generally excluded.

Coordinate bounded reviews, keeping shared browser sessions serialized. Support recommendations with concrete user consequences, screenshots where useful, implementation references, acceptance criteria, and validation needs. Check design-system ownership and only use competitor examples for demonstrated, contained gaps. Independently verify findings, record inaccessible or unverified areas, and prioritize small implementation slices with cross-functional handoffs.

This is an editorial summary. Read the linked gist for the complete workflow.

prompts.title: Review last week's sessions and suggest improvements
prompts.use_when: Recent coding sessions are available and the user wants to identify ways to improve their workflow.
prompts.prompt: look at last weeks sessions and suggest improvements

prompts.title: Map the codebase into ARCHITECTURE.md
prompts.use_when: A project has grown messy and you want a written map of its structure, data flow, and riskiest files.
prompts.prompt: Map this codebase for me. Show the folder structure, what each main file does, how data flows from UI to database, and the 5 riskiest files to touch. Write it all to ARCHITECTURE.md.

prompts.title: Audit and prune old AI agent transcripts on macOS
prompts.use_when: The user wants to review and remove old coding-agent transcripts, session logs, and leftover editor folders on a Mac.
prompts.prompt: Audit my Mac for AI agent transcripts (Claude, Codex, Cursor, Grok), SQLite session logs, and leftover editor dotfolders older than 30 days. Show me the sizes first, delete everything >30 days old, and add a daily 30-day auto-prune check.

prompts.title: Find and fix happy-path debt in your app
prompts.use_when: An app works in the demo but breaks on slow loads, failures, empty lists, long text, or narrow screens.
prompts.prompt: Find all the happy-path debt in my app: every screen that only works when data loads fast, nothing fails, lists aren't empty, text is short, and the screen is wide. Fix missing states and layout breaks, one component at a time, without changing my design and without breaking anything. Summarize by file: what happened before vs. how it works now.

prompts.title: Fresh-eyes due-diligence audit of a live domain
prompts.use_when: The user wants an outside-in check of a live site or product, run from an empty folder with no repo access, to catch broken links, stale subdomains, and sloppy public pages.
prompts.prompt: Visit [domain] like a strict enterprise buyer doing due diligence. Check DNS records, every footer/legal link, public JS bundles, and onboarding pages, and give me a checklist of anything broken or sloppy.

prompts.title: Check whether you load third-party JS that could be compromised
prompts.use_when: A third-party script provider has been compromised and you want to know if your site is exposed to a similar attack.
prompts.prompt:
Read this incident: https://x.com/Scott_Helme/status/2122422157959471456

Help me understand what the root cause of this issue is.
Do we load any third-party JS that would be susceptible to a similar attack (if that third-party JS provider were compromised)?

prompts.title: Plan logging that can replay what the user experienced
prompts.use_when: You want a program to produce logs good enough to later analyze for broken behavior and user friction.
prompts.prompt: help me plan comprehensive logging such that we can replay what the user experienced, meaningful internal operations, and visible outcomes

prompts.title: Review your agent setup for guardrail gaps
prompts.use_when: You want a one-off review of your AGENTS.md, skills, hooks, permissions and MCP setup.
prompts.prompt: Review my entire agent setup: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, skills, commands, subagents, hooks, settings/permissions, and MCP servers. Check for gaps in guardrails and whether it follows current best practices for Fable 5.2.

prompts.title: Estimate what your Claude Code usage would cost on the API
prompts.use_when: The user wants a local, offline-safe report of what their Claude Code sessions over a time frame would have cost at Anthropic's API list prices, with an HTML summary card.
prompts.prompt:
Time frame: 30d

Work out what my Claude Code sessions in this time frame would cost if I had paid for
them on the Claude API at Anthropic's list prices. Use only Python's standard library
and do it in one script you write to a temporary folder. Do not send my logs or any
results anywhere.

1. **Prices.** Fetch `https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing.md`
   (the public pricing page, as Markdown). From the "Model pricing" table take, per
   model, the USD per million tokens for: base input, 5-minute cache write, 1-hour
   cache write, cache read and output. From the "Fast mode pricing" section take the
   fast-mode input and output price per model; fast-mode cache prices are the base
   cache prices scaled by fast input divided by base input. Take the web search price
   per 1,000 searches. Never guess or hard-code a rate. If the page cannot be fetched,
   stop and tell me.

2. **Usage.** Read every `*.jsonl` file under `~/.claude/projects/`, recursively, so
   subagent logs under `<project>/<session>/subagents/` count too and belong to their
   parent project. Each line is JSON. Keep lines whose `message.usage` and
   `message.model` are set, skipping the model `<synthetic>`. A reply is written as
   several lines that stream, so its usage is only final on the last one: treat each
   `(message.id, requestId)` pair as one reply and keep each usage field's largest
   value across its lines, not the first line's. Use the first line's `timestamp`
   (ISO, UTC) and keep only replies inside the time frame, counted back from now
   (`all` means everything; a month is 30.44 days).

   Claude Code deletes logs after its cleanup period (30 days by default). If the
   time frame starts before the oldest log, estimate the missing days from
   `~/.claude/stats-cache.json` (what /stats shows): `dailyModelTokens` has tokens
   per day per model, `modelUsage` has each model's split by token type (use it to
   split a day's tokens), `dailyActivity` has sessions per day. /stats adds up every
   log line, so it counts each reply several times. Measure that overcount on the
   full days that have both logs and cache (cache tokens divided by log tokens, all
   types summed) and divide the missing days by it. Never hard-code the ratio. Price
   the estimate's cache writes at the 5-minute rate, so it is a lower bound. If the
   file is missing or no day has both, skip the estimate and say why.

3. **Price each reply** at the rate of the model that wrote it. Map the model id to
   the pricing table by dropping a trailing `[...]`, a leading `claude-`, any
   `anthropic.`/`us.anthropic.` prefix and a date suffix (`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`
   is Haiku 4.5; old ids like `claude-3-5-haiku` are Haiku 3.5). From `usage`:
   - `input_tokens` at the input rate, `output_tokens` at the output rate,
     `cache_read_input_tokens` at the cache read rate;
   - `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens` and `ephemeral_1h_input_tokens` at the
     5-minute and 1-hour write rates; if both are missing, put all of
     `cache_creation_input_tokens` at the 5-minute rate;
   - `speed == "fast"` means fast-mode rates;
   - `server_tool_use.web_search_requests` at the web search price.
   A model with no list price is left out of the total and listed as unpriced.

4. **Tell me:** the total API cost for the time frame, the number of sessions
   (distinct `sessionId`) and replies, the split by cache reads, cache writes, output,
   fresh input and web searches (tokens and dollars each), cost by model, the top six
   projects (the project is the log's folder name under `~/.claude/projects/`), any
   unpriced models, and the date the prices were fetched. If part of it is the
   estimate, say how much, for which dates, and the overcount you divided by;
   projects and per-day cover the logged days only.

5. **Card.** Write the same figures as one self-contained HTML page to
   `~/api-bill/api-bill-<timeframe>-<date>.html` and give me the path: the total in
   large type, the itemised split as a receipt, bars for cost by model and by
   project, a bar chart of cost per day, and a table of the prices used, and the
   estimate (if any) marked as one. Start the page with `<!doctype html>`,
   `<meta charset="utf-8">` and a viewport meta tag, so symbols such as "·" and "×"
   show correctly when opened locally. Make it readable on a phone and in dark mode. If you can publish Artifacts in this
   session, offer to publish the card as a private page. It shows my project names,
   so never make it public.

Do not compare with my subscription price. This is what the same work would cost on
the API, nothing more.
